concepts.label: all_channels property (computed, read-only)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the read-only, computed union of a user's or role's own admin_channels, its access()-derived grants, and (for a user) every role's own all_channels; distinct from sgw:admin-channels-property, which is the settable input field, not the computed effective-access output. This page is the fullest single statement of the computation and is where it belongs.

relations.subject: sgw:all-channels-property
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate - the first of three named sources the computed all_channels union draws from
relations.evidence: The user's `admin_channels` property, which is set using the Admin REST API.

relations.subject: sgw:all-channels-property
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate - the second named source
relations.evidence: The channels the user has been granted access to by [access()](sync-function/sync-function-api-access-cmd.md) calls from sync functions invoked for current revisions of documents.

relations.subject: sgw:all-channels-property
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate - the third named source: a user's effective channel set recursively includes every role's own computed all_channels
relations.evidence: The `all_channels` properties of any roles the user belongs to. These are themselves computed using the above rules.

relations.subject: sgw:all-channels-property
relations.evidence:
Use the Admin REST API to see the:

* Channels a user has access to
* Channels a role has access to
* Channels a document is assigned to

relations.subject: sgw:role
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted relation, restated here with this page's own worked example
relations.evidence: hoopy through the froods role's admin\_channels setting in the default collection.

notable_absence.finding: This page's three-endpoint worked example (GET _user/pupshaw, GET _role/frood, GET _all_docs?channels=true) traces the entire access chain concretely in one place: the document ourdoc is assigned to channel hoopy via channel(); the role froods is granted hoopy via admin_channels; the user pupshaw belongs to role froods and therefore inherits hoopy into its own all_channels. The page states the causal chain explicitly: 'That assignment to hoopy is what makes it available to our froods role and therefore to our user pupshaw.' This is the clearest end-to-end illustration in the whole corpus (across both this round and round 3) of the full grantsChannelAccess + inheritsAccessFromRole + routesDocumentToChannel chain resolving to an actual read decision, and is worth flagging to reconciliation as strong corroborating evidence for keeping those three relations distinct rather than collapsing them.

cross_component_finding: There is no equivalent 'verify effective access' read-only introspection endpoint documented for server/'s RBAC model or Capella's role model in this corpus so far - both of those models are checked implicitly at operation time (privilege lookup, role-gated API call) rather than exposed as a queryable computed union a caller can inspect ahead of time. Sync Gateway's all_channels property, by contrast, is presented as a first-class debugging/verification surface precisely because the effective access set is itself a non-trivial computed union across three sources (own admin_channels, dynamic access() grants, and inherited role grants) that cannot be read off any single stored field - the docs treat 'what can this user actually see' as a question worth its own dedicated how-to page, which is a structural signal that SGW's channel model is harder to reason about statically than a fixed privilege/role lookup.
